key_insight: ID-MAE learns to predict driver impairment while also reconstructing missing gaze and trajectory data. This combines impairment prediction with self-supervised learning to address the high cost of labeling drivers’ cognitive states.
problem_solved: Driver cognitive states interact subtly with gaze, behavior, and the driving environment, but obtaining ground-truth labels at scale is expensive.
method: Use a multimodal masked-diffusion autoencoder to model driver impairment alongside gaze and trajectory.
Predict the impairment label as a masked token.
Add a self-supervised objective that reconstructs masked gaze and trajectory data.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the approach offers a way to pair costly supervision with learning signals from multimodal driving data. The provided abstract is incomplete, so performance gains and label-efficiency improvements cannot be confirmed.

paper_title: Multimodal Masked Diffusion Autoencoder for Modeling Impaired Driving
paper_authors: John Gideon, Anshul Gupta, Megan Applegate-Kenton, Kayli Battel, Todd J Rowell
